title: Quasi-holonomy in non-adiabatic quantum evolution
abstract: We develop a framework for quasi-holonomy in non-adiabatic quantum time evolution of subspaces along loops in a complex Grassmannian. By factoring the Schrödinger evolution into dynamical and connection-induced contributions in a moving basis, we obtain an effective geometric generator that depends explicitly on the dynamical propagator. This quasi-connection does not define a genuine connection on the original Grassmann bundle, since its gauge transformation law acquires a history-dependent, nonlocal term. Other ways of factoring the Schrödinger evolution are briefly discussed. All these approaches suffer from the same type of history-dependence, thereby defining transport of subspaces in which geometric and dynamical effects are generally intertwined, just as in the case of the quasi-holonomy. Our work sheds light on the issue of separating quantum evolution of subspaces into holonomic and dynamical parts from an essentially gauge-theoretic perspective.
summary: This paper develops a framework to analyze how quantum subspaces evolve over time by factoring the Schrödinger equation into dynamical and geometric parts. The authors demonstrate that this separation fails because the resulting 'quasi-connection' retains a history-dependent term, proving that geometry and dynamics are fundamentally intertwined in this setting. This offers a deep gauge-theoretic understanding of non-adiabatic subspace evolution.
main_problem: The central problem is investigating whether the quantum time evolution of subspaces can be cleanly separated into purely geometric (holonomic) and dynamical components.
main_result: The authors show that this separation fails in general because the effective quasi-connection depends explicitly on the history of the dynamical propagator, indicating an inherent intertwining of geometric and dynamic effects.
method: They develop a framework by factoring the Schrödinger evolution into dynamical and connection-induced parts using a moving basis along paths in the complex Grassmannian.
model_or_system: The model concerns the time evolution of $M$-dimensional subspaces within an $N$-dimensional Hilbert space, mathematically described as paths on the complex Grassmannian $	ext{Gr}(N; M)$ governed by a matrix differential equation.
key_observables: The quasi-connection $	ext{AD}(t)$, which is used to diagnose the failure of separation from standard connection forms.
important_parameters: Cyclic evolution (loops) and the time dependence of the Hamiltonian/generators $K(t)$ and $A(t)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on factoring the propagator using a moving basis, but the core limitation is the history-dependence of the resulting quasi-connection.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem via the Schrödinger equation factorization, derives the quasi-holonomy generator $	ext{AD}(t)$, proves it fails to be a true connection due to history dependence, and discusses conditions under which separation might occur (e.g., commutativity).
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous geometric/gauge-theoretic perspective on open quantum systems dynamics, directly addressing the fundamental question of separability in time evolution that is crucial for understanding decoherence or adiabatic approximations.
